title: Malleable Evals: Why Are We Evaluating Adaptive Systems with Static Tests? — Vincent Koc, OpenClaw
talk_summary: Vincent Koc argues that static benchmarks and handcrafted eval suites are mismatched to adaptive agent harnesses that change themselves, and proposes evals as living, agent-maintained artifacts. He sketches mechanisms: self-curated suites from production traces, always-on online evaluation, and telemetry-in-the-loop self-correction toward intent-defined end states.

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents mine production traces for recurring and newly emerging behaviors, then generate/update the eval suite themselves instead of humans hand-writing static cases.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We can self-curate suites from traces, as in not me, but the agent can

takeaways.what_they_do: Run evaluation continuously against live traffic rather than only offline before deploy, so drift in inputs surfaces as eval signal.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We can do online always-on evaluation optimizations.

takeaways.what_they_do: Make the harness aware of its own telemetry (errors, cost) with set conditions so it can self-correct and continue rather than fail the run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the harness is aware of the telemetry it's aware of like what's breaking, it's aware of like how much it's costing

takeaways.what_they_do: Define the desired end state/outcome and let the machine optimize toward it, rather than comparing against a fixed expected answer dataset.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our evals become like what is the end state that we want to get to and then we just let the machines do the work

takeaways.technique: Adaptive/selective testing focus on the changing 20%
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat ~80% as stable static checks and concentrate adaptive eval effort on the ~20% of behavior that keeps changing and breaks the business.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that 20% is always going to keep changing and it's that 20% that's going to mess up your business
